title.narrative: The Horn of Africa Regional Programme (HARP Phase Three), 2025 – 2028
The Horn of Africa Regional Programme (HARP Phase Three), 2025 – 2028

description.narrative: HARP aims to elevate the voices, and transforming the circumstances, of the most peripheral and excluded groups in the Horn of Africa. The programme aims to do this by focusing on women, youth, and other marginalised groups, and connecting them to decision-making on a set of key human security issues and linking policy actors to the experiences of excluded communities.

HARP syftar till att förstärka rösterna och förändra villkoren för de mest perifera och exkluderade grupperna på Afrikas horn. Programmet syftar till att göra detta genom att fokusera på kvinnor, ungdomar och andra marginaliserade grupper och koppla dem till beslutsfattande om en rad viktiga frågor som rör mänsklig säkerhet samt koppla politiska aktörer till de exkluderade samhällenas och gruppernas egna erfarenheter.

The overall objective of the Project is Centring the Peripheries and Marginalised: Historically excluded and emerging civil society actors influence regional policies and policy processes related to peace and security towards greater alignment with community needs and aspirations. With in this general objective, the program works towards three outcome/ specific objectives.
Outcome 1 Secure and Prosperous Borderlands: Borderland communities influence policy responses to security and development in their contexts, and promote more relevant, effective, and inclusive regional policy implementation in and across borders.
Outcome 2 Inclusive Decision-Making on Transitional Justice and Reconciliation: Local civil society actors in the Horn of Africa influence regional transitional justice and reconciliation processes, enhancing collective ownership and the relevance and effectiveness of key policy frameworks.
Outcome 3 Unheard Voices on Climate: Regional decision-making on climate, peace, and security is influenced by local experiences of the impact of climate change on conflict and livelihoods across the Horn of Africa

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

title.narrative: Grant agreement THE HORN OF AFRICA REGIONAL PROGRAMME (HARP PHASE THREE), 2025 – 2028
Decision on contribution THE HORN OF AFRICA REGIONAL PROGRAMME (HARP PHASE THREE), 2025 – 2028 , 17390

description.narrative:
Despite the delayed start of HARP 3.0, LPI achieved several foundational results across all three outcome areas. Under Outcome 1 (Secure and Prosperous Borderlands), LPI reactivated and strengthened partnerships with borderland civil society actors, including the newly rebranded Eastern Africa Borderlands Civil Society Platform. Partners reported that skills gained through LPIs earlier support translated into continued peacebuilding activities, demonstrating early behavioural change among community actors. LPI also completed a lessonslearned report from the Karamoja Cluster Small Grants and initiated alignment work with the Moyale crossborder resilience project, laying the groundwork for harmonised regional policy engagement.
Under Outcome 2 (Inclusive DecisionMaking on Transitional Justice and Reconciliation), LPI supported national and subnational CSOs to contextualise and engage with the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP). Collaboration with IGAD and the AU remained strong, enabling local actorssuch as African Women for Transitional Justice (AW4TJ)to access regional decisionmaking spaces. Preparations for crosscohort learning and countryspecific TJR research products advanced, contributing to increased knowledge, coordination, and readiness among civil society actors to influence regional transitional justice processes.
Under Outcome 3 (Unheard Voices on Climate), LPI generated and validated new knowledge on climateinduced urban migration in Baidoa and Kisumu. The research involved both community actors and policymakers, and the validated findings were published as a policy brief intended to inform regional climatepeacesecurity discussions. This represents an early example of evidencebased influence on policy actors and demonstrates LPIs ability to convene multistakeholder processes around climaterelated security issues.
Across all outcomes, LPI strengthened relationships with key regional institutionsincluding IGAD, AUC/PAPS, and PBSOand ensured meaningful participation of community partners in highlevel dialogues (e.g., Kampala peacekeeping discussions, Geneva CSO Dialogue). These engagements contributed to desirable changes by increasing the visibility, legitimacy, and influence of local civil society actors in regional policy arenas. The initiation of a gender analysis, baseline study, and regional context analysis further positions the programme for stronger results measurement and strategic influence in 2026.
